beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Google has quietly made AI video free for everyone. But the real question isn't whether you can make video clips for free. It's how you spend them.

show.event: types 'Can I make a whole video'
backspaces 'a whole video' → 'video clips' on the spoken correction

props.text:
Can I make a whole video
with AI for free?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive whole-video question and corrects it to the real one: how to spend free clips.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. Vids: Google's video app, which opens at vids.new. Veo: the AI model that turns a sentence into a video clip. And the free tier: a free monthly allowance of clips — the current number is at vids.new.

terms.meaning: Google's video app — it opens at vids.new
the AI model that turns a sentence into a video clip
a free monthly allowance of clips (current number at vids.new)

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Google Vids is Google's video app. It opens at vids.new, and earlier this year it grew an AI clip maker: you type a sentence, and Veo turns it into a short, high-definition video clip.

shot.visual_intent: A browser window with a dark title bar, label 'vids.new'; a film-clip frame grows out of it with a terracotta spark.

show.event: clip frame grows out of the window

shot.motion_claim: A browser window with a dark title bar, label 'vids.new'; a film-clip frame grows out of it with a terracotta spark.

beats.narration_text: The unit is the clip: one short shot, a few seconds long, in high definition. Think of each clip as a single shot in your video — never the whole video.

beats.narration_text: A personal Google account gets a free monthly allowance of these clips. It isn't unlimited: treat it as a small monthly budget, and it refills each month.

shot.visual_intent: A kraft budget jar labelled 'free tier'; three clip boxes drop into it, one per spoken beat.
shot.motion_claim: A kraft budget jar labelled 'free tier'; three clip boxes drop into it, one per spoken beat.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Spend each clip where AI video wins: a shot you could never film yourself and won't find in stock footage. A drone flight over a volcano. A scene from history. A product shot that doesn't exist yet.

shot.visual_intent: A clip frame holding a stylized volcano (dark silhouette, terracotta glow); an ink check lands; label 'AI wins'.
shot.motion_claim: A clip frame holding a stylized volcano (dark silhouette, terracotta glow); an ink check lands; label 'AI wins'.

beats.narration_text: Don't spend them on the generic stuff: a sunset, coffee pouring, hands typing. Vids comes with free stock footage — use stock for that, and keep your clips for the shots only AI can make.

shot.visual_intent: An open stock box with film strips, label 'stock'; the free-tier jar sits beside it, untouched.
shot.motion_claim: An open stock box with film strips, label 'stock'; the free-tier jar sits beside it, untouched.

beats.narration_text: Plan before you spend. Write the video in Vids first: the script, the scenes, the shot list. Then spend clips only on the hero shots, and let stock cover everything else.

shot.visual_intent: Two script pages; a timeline with three slots; one AI clip drops into the hero slot, stock strips into the others; label 'script first'.
shot.motion_claim: Two script pages; a timeline with three slots; one AI clip drops into the hero slot, stock strips into the others; label 'script first'.

beats.narration_text: Like a clip but want it longer? Extend it — grow the scene instead of starting over. You can also test several prompts at once. Just remember: every try spends one clip from the jar.

shot.visual_intent: A clip frame elongates to double width (extend arrow); a prompt pill spawns two test clips; one clip leaves the budget jar; label 'extend'.

beats.narration_text: The free tier covers clips. The extras — custom AI music, avatars that read your script — need a paid plan. Skip them for now: Vids ships with free stock music and voices, and nothing here stops your first video.

shot.visual_intent: The free-tier jar with its clips; two dim cards 'music' and 'avatar' sit greyed behind it; label 'paid extras'.
shot.motion_claim: The free-tier jar with its clips; two dim cards 'music' and 'avatar' sit greyed behind it; label 'paid extras'.

beats.narration_text: One last thing. The free number has already moved before, and Google hasn't promised it stays put. Before you plan a video, check vids.new for the current limit — never plan around a number from a film.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Help me plan a 30-second announcement video for [my cause]: a one-paragraph script, a shot list, and mark each shot as AI clip or stock footage — AI clips only for shots I can't film or find in stock. End with the three hero shots I should generate first. Then check two things yourself. Is every AI clip a shot you couldn't film or find in stock? And did you check vids.new for the current free number before generating?
